issues.legal_issue: An arbitral tribunal may terminate proceedings under Section 32(2)(c) only when, on material in the record, it is satisfied that continuing them has become unnecessary or impossible.
An arbitral tribunal has a duty to fix hearings and adjudicate the referred dispute even if the parties do not request a hearing date.
A claimant’s failure to request a hearing date, by itself, does not make arbitral proceedings unnecessary or establish abandonment of the claim.
A claimant’s abandonment of a claim may justify termination under Section 32(2)(c), but implied abandonment requires convincing evidence permitting no other inference.
The record did not establish that the claimant had abandoned its claim, so termination of the arbitral proceedings under Section 32(2)(c) was illegal.
